evals.expected_output: Quick-notes mode. States it is critiquing code only, not footage. Reads the CSS as a motion spec and diagnoses 'laggy' mechanically (symmetric ease-in-out on a frequent entrance, 600 ms for a 420 px travel, stagger tax pushing the last row to ~1 s, delay doing choreography work, no interruption or reduced-motion handling). Notes follow observation, perceptual effect, why, concrete change with values, preserve. Cites frequency (30 opens/day) as the reason for a tighter budget. Asks for a screen recording or the rapid open/close behavior to confirm retrigger behavior.

evals.prompt:
Review my lower third for our evening news open. 1080i59.94 in AE, 30 fps comp. Name bar and text keyframes:

Bar position X: f0 (-900) -> f12 (0), both keyframes easy ease 33% influence
Name text opacity: f6 0% -> f14 100%, linear
Name text position X: f6 (+40) -> f14 (0), easy ease 33%
Title line opacity: f10 0% -> f18 100%, linear
Hold: f18 -> f78 (60 frames)
Out: bar position X f78 (0) -> f90 (-900), easy ease 33%; text opacity f78 100% -> f84 0%

It's used for guests with names from 8 to 34 characters and titles up to 60 characters. Full review please, with the scorecard. I'm mostly worried it looks flat and that long titles get cut off too fast.
evals.expected_output: Full-review mode in the broadcast dialect, flagged as such, with the corpus's product-UI bias acknowledged where relevant. States it is analyzing keyframe values and cannot see the render. Computes read time against the fixed 60-frame (2 s) hold for a 60-character title and finds it short; flags that the hold is fixed rather than length-driven; notes symmetric 33% easy ease on a 12-frame travel, identical in and out (entrance arrives and exit departs with the same profile), linear fades, bar and text effectively unsynchronized as a group (common fate), exit timing, safe areas and legibility at distance (asks for confirmation), interlaced field/motion considerations, no flash risk but notes the check. Provides the 12-dimension scorecard with 'not assessable' where evidence is missing and a revision hypothesis for each score of 3 or below. Gives concrete values (e.g., asymmetric influences, a hold formula tied to character count, offsets in frames) and a preserve clause. Lists what to capture for a better review (speed graph screenshot, 0.25x render).

evals.prompt: my team's logo reveal for our new sub-brand feels cheap and I can't say why. it's about 4 seconds, logo builds up from shapes and then there's a flare and a bounce at the end. can you tell me what's probably wrong and how I should talk to the designer about it? she's pretty junior and I don't want to crush her.
evals.expected_output: Does not pretend to have seen the animation; says it is working from a description and lists what to capture (0.25x screen recording, speed-graph screenshot, the audio). Converts 'cheap' into ranked, testable hypotheses (default or symmetric easing, uniform timing with no hero beat, flare and bounce as unearned overshoot/polish, weak or missing hold and resolution, generic reveal that fails the strip-it distinctiveness test) with a quick test for each. Then gives team-critique framing: start from her intent, observation before judgment, mechanism-level language, one change as a testable hypothesis with a preserve clause, a small mentoring exercise (e.g., curve decomposition or reduce to the single most important move), and phrasings that keep it kind and specific. Offers calibrate or a full review as a follow-up rather than doing everything unprompted.

evals.prompt: Here's a 6 second MP4 of our new channel logo sting (attached as sting.mp4). Does the motion feel right? Be specific.
evals.expected_output: Probes the exact frame rate with ffprobe and extracts every frame with ffmpeg before any timing verdict; measures positions across the full sequence; notes where motion blur makes positions uncertain and avoids verdicts it cannot measure; never judges timing from a handful of sampled frames. If extraction is impossible, says so and limits itself to composition, type and colour.

evals.prompt: Our end credits roll looks broken. It's 1080p at 23.976, white type in a thin sans on black, and the roll moves 1440 px over 1080 frames. The thin strokes keep flickering and the whole thing looks stuttery. I already tried rendering again with a higher bitrate and it's the same. What's going on and what values should I change?
evals.expected_output: Rules out playback first (a re-render at a higher bitrate that still stutters points to the speed, not the data rate). Computes the speed as 1.333 px per frame and separates its two symptoms: thin strokes pulsing in brightness as they straddle pixel rows (sub-pixel rendering, phase cycle repeating every 3 frames) and an uneven 1-2-1 cadence if positions snap to whole pixels; ideally runs scripts/move_speed.py. Gives concrete fixes with values: a whole-pixel speed (1 px/frame over 1440 frames, or 2 px/frame over 720 frames) chosen against the required running time, a heavier weight or larger size for thin strokes, motion blur as an option, and notes that 23.976 is the worst case for judder. Does not blame the codec or ask for a better export as the main fix.

evals.prompt: Notes on our 3D logo open before it goes to the client: a chrome team logo sits on a dark stage. Pucks fly in from frame left and smash into it, shards spray out, then the camera pushes in for the lockup. Frames 40-60: the shards seem to come out of the logo's face rather than off where the pucks hit, and two pucks pass a few frames inside the logo before they bounce. The logo also sits a few pixels above the stage floor with no shadow under it. At frame 72 the camera starts its push-in from a dead stop with a linear ramp and the key light jumps from 40% to 100% over 2 frames. The spot follows a replay clip in the edit and starts on a black frame. What are your notes?
evals.expected_output: Names the physical-plausibility failures as one family (the solid logo is penetrated, debris originates from the wrong place, the logo floats with no contact cue) and prescribes fixes: collision on the logo, debris emitted from the impact point with varied direction and timing, the logo grounded with a contact shadow or settle. Calls the camera start and the 2-frame light jump harsh and prescribes a long ease-in and an arcing sweep for the camera and a gradual fade for the light, with frame or percent values. Flags the black frame as a dead gap at the cut and asks for the transition to be reviewed against the outgoing replay clip, carrying motion across. Recommends checking the contact frames frame by frame. Includes a preserve clause and ranks notes by impact.
